clue.text: Hard after Ed Balls on the outside, almost certain to win

indicators.note: one piece is placed following another, so the word for hard comes next in line
the word for nonsense sits around the other letters, wrapping them like a shell

blocks.note: balls is nonsense, ROT; its first two letters open the wrapper
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
the last letter of ROT closes the wrapper

explanation.surface: Ed Balls, the Labour politician, is mocked as a hard man who only looks a sure winner from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls means rubbish, ROT, which goes around ED followed by H.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-hot favourite is a contender whom bookmakers rate as nearly sure of victory.

explanation.definitionFit: Plum duff is a boiled or steamed fruit pudding, a dessert, which is a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Bolshie, Sweeney Todd-style?

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is invented: a strop is the leather strap a barber hones a cut-throat razor on, and Sweeney Todd is the demon barber of Fleet Street. Bolshie is British slang for rebellious.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroppy is British slang for bad-tempered and uncooperative, which is what bolshie means too.

clue.text: Prick welcoming Labour's leader before party reverse, remains a prick

one piece is placed ahead of the next

first letter of Labour

explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Prick' is CHOPPER, holding L and OD; the second is the definition, in the sense of an oaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy, oafish person, and calling someone a prick is a cruder insult of the same kind.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eff-off' reads as a mild swear, but it splits into the letters EFF and the signal word off.
explanation.definitionFit: In effect means in practice or as things actually stand, the same as saying how it turns out.

clue.text: (& 23dn.) Subject: nabbing rich, proud bastard protecting those coarse people in disgraced organisation

indicators.note: bastard as an adjective means debased or irregular, so the letters are corrupted into a new order
to nab is to grab hold of, so the first word takes the rest inside
to protect is to surround and shield, so the jumbled letters wrap the short word

blocks.note: a theme is a subject
the nine letters to rearrange
'em is a coarse way of saying them, those people

explanation.surface: A satirical take on a press scandal: a rich, proud bastard shielding coarse people inside a disgraced organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those coarse people' is them said coarsely, dropping the TH. The puzzle appeared in 2011, at the height of the News of the World phone-hacking scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Murdoch's media group, News Corporation, was publicly disgraced by the News of the World phone-hacking scandal.

explanation.definitionFit: Lavatorial humour is crude comedy about bodily functions and toilets, also called toilet humour.

clue.text: Succeed in getting sexual partner before balls woolly

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, to pull is to succeed in getting a partner; an over in cricket is six balls bowled. A woolly is a knitted jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullover is a knitted sweater, and a woolly is British for a knitted garment of the same kind.
